hold_text: R12, and this time the condition is MET rather than assumed: the diff modifies .github/workflows/pr-opener.yml and scripts/ops/session_registry.py, both named on check_pr_landing.py's LANDING_MACHINERY list that R8 verifies against the diff. It also changes .github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml, which is the arming path for every machine-generated PR. A change to the landing route may not land itself -- the change and its own approval would be the same act, and a mistake in it disarms the check that would have caught the mistake. Concretely here: this PR flips pr-opener.yml's `draft` default to false, so a mistake would open every future session PR ready when it meant to hold one. One human read.
why: Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list (GitHub Actions workflow fixes, CI scripts, ops scripts, docs). MI-98 has two halves, both from operator rulings on 2026-09-03. (a) THE AUTOMATION LOCKOUT: .github/actions/commit-to-main now writes its own .github/pr-landing/<slug>.json and .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt, so machine-generated PRs make the same declaration every other PR makes. Deliberately NOT an automation/** exemption in the guard, which would have created an unguarded lane on the guard's first day. PROVEN against a real red-locked branch (automation/reconcile-open-prs-33730997737-1): the guard moved from `R11 no landing declaration` to `OK -- state=declared_self_land`. (b) DRAFTS STOP BEING A HOLD: pr-opener.yml's draft default flips to false and the spawn template stops telling Tier-2/3 sessions to stay drafts; a PR is held by its landing declaration instead. VERIFIED before relying on it that the declaration is load-bearing -- claude-pr-automerge arms only on the request file, and R10 fails an armed PR that declares hold. No src/, no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps, no deploy/, no live-VM runtime file.
